reconcile.note: Clarke harmonizes the accounts by casting Salome as spokesperson for her sons while Jesus, aware of the true petitioners, answers James and John directly.

discrepancy.note: Strauss identifies the same episode with two competing petitioners, the sons in Mark and their mother in Matthew, as an unharmonized doublet in the tradition.

quotes.text: These disciples (according to Mark), or their mother for them (according to Matthew), petitioned for the two first places next to Jesus in the messianic kingdom
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), on Matthew 20:21 and Mark 10:37.

sides.snippet: Command that these, my two sons, may sit, one on your right hand, and one on your left hand, in your Kingdom.
sides.verseText: He said to her, \"What do you want?\" She said to him, \"Command that these, my two sons, may sit, one on your right hand, and one on your left hand, in your Kingdom.\"

sides.snippet: Grant to us that we may sit, one at your right hand, and one at your left hand, in your glory.
sides.verseText: They said to him, \"Grant to us that we may sit, one at your right hand, and one at your left hand, in your glory.\"
